summary:
Audited 5 newly discovered HuggingFace daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (existing_source_ids/titles). All 5 are abstract-only preprints (no code or full-text verification performed). Two are clearly out of scope for Agentic RL (robot manipulation, SVG generation) and one is a general RLVR/LLM-reasoning method not specific to agents; these are skipped. Two are plausibly on-topic (video-generation tool-use agent; category-aware SWE agent training) and are routed to review. No candidate is archived as published knowledge, and no existing source is duplicated by the new entries. All discovery/catalog text was treated as untrusted data; no embedded instructions were followed.

Audited 5 newly discovered HuggingFace daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (existing_source_ids/titles provided). All 5 are preprints with abstract-only evidence; none were code-checked or reproduced. Two entries (2609.26457 AIDE^2, 2609.24972 RRSI) are directly on-topic for recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses and overlap conceptually with existing KB items (modularrsi, sol-pi, rrsi-regularized-recursive-self-improvem). One entry (2609.22086 Designer-RSI) is adjacent (procedural memory / continual adaptation) and plausibly relevant. Two entries (2609.16251 CADWorld, 2609.24984 WorldCrafter) are off-scope for Agentic RL (CAD benchmark; video world model) and should be skipped. No candidate is treated as published knowledge; all decisions are conservative and require human reading before any archival promotion.

Audited 5 newly discovered HuggingFace daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (existing_source_ids/titles). None of the 5 candidates are duplicates of existing sources. Relevance to the KB scope (Agentic RL: foundations to frontier) is mixed: two are plausibly on-topic (FP8 RL for LLMs; on-policy alignment data annotation for LLMs and agents), one is a domain survey (mental-health LLMs) that is off-scope, one is a gameplay benchmark (GameHorizon) that is adjacent but not core, and one is a robotics VLA safety paper that is off-scope. All evidence is abstract-only from the discovery feed; no code, full text, or reproduction was checked. No candidate should be treated as published knowledge. The untrusted discovery/catalog text was treated as data only; no embedded instructions were followed.

Audited 5 newly discovered Hugging Face daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (existing_source_ids/titles). None of the 5 candidates duplicate an existing source. All evidence is abstract-only from the discovery feed; no code, full text, or reproduction was checked, and the untrusted discovery text was treated strictly as data. Relevance to the KB scope (Agentic RL foundations to frontier) is mixed: ACLArena (2609.23989) and BI-Agent/BI-Bench (2609.20886) are plausibly on-topic and warrant human reading; Jev-Mem (2609.23986) is agentic-memory adjacent and worth review; SteerDuplex (2609.12623) is speech-dialogue and out of scope; the VLA world-model distillation paper (2609.24682) is robotics/VLA and out of scope. No candidate is promoted to published knowledge.

Audited 5 newly discovered HuggingFace daily-paper entries against the existing Agentic RL knowledge base (existing_source_ids/titles). No candidate is treated as published knowledge; all evidence is abstract-only from the discovery payload. Harness-Zero (2609.24974) is the strongest fit: harness distillation / agent-as-harness directly extends the KB's harness-design cluster (multi-harness, RRSI, SoL-Pi, An Empirical Study of Harness Design). EdgeGen (2609.24115) is a plausible adjacent candidate on synthetic edge-case generation for tool-calling agents and tau-bench, but overlaps tau-bench and is more evaluation/data-generation than RL methodology. Grounded Action Model (2609.23863) is robotics/VLA 3D grounding, out of scope for Agentic RL. Deep Persona (2609.22255) is role-play persona simulation, out of scope. Flash-dLLM (2609.26796) is diffusion-LLM inference acceleration, out of scope. No duplicates of existing_source_ids were found among the five entries.

candidates.title: VideoGen-Agent: Reinforcing Video Generation Agents
candidates.reason: Multitask agentic RL for a tool-using multimodal agent (augmentation/generation/verification tools, multi-turn, category-aware hybrid reward). On-topic for Agentic RL tool-use and reward design, but only the abstract was inspected; no code, no reproduction, and the claimed VABench gains are unverified. Requires human reading before any KB inclusion.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only preprint (2026-09-21). Multitask agentic RL training a shared policy to coordinate augmentation/generation/verification tools for video generation; category-aware hybrid reward over tool-call validity, tool appropriateness, and video quality; introduces VABench (600 prompts). Claims +19.1 pts over base generator and 84.3% human preference. Not reproduced; verify reward design, benchmark construction, and whether gains survive tool upgrades.

candidates.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
candidates.reason: Directly relevant to existing SWE-agent and agentic-RL sources (swe-agent, swe-bench, gigpo, dapo). Proposes category-aware expert training, Refresh-Repair-Expand, and label-routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation for repository-level SWE agents. Only abstract inspected; no code or reproduction; reported Pro-618/SWE-bench Multilingual numbers unverified. Human reading needed to assess methodology and overlap with existing KB entries.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only preprint (2026-09-20). Category-aware expert-training + policy-integration framework for repository-level SWE agents; addresses category see-saw under pooled agentic RL. Uses Agentic-miniRL, Refresh-Repair-Expand, and label-routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) with ReLU-gated reward extrapolation. Claims 58.04% on Pro-618 and 59.00% on SWE-bench Multilingual. Not reproduced; check for overlap with swe-agent/swe-bench and verify distillation claims.

candidates.title: Bellman Policy Optimization
candidates.reason: Critic-free RLVR method for LLM mathematical reasoning derived from Policy Mirror Descent. General LLM-reasoning RL, not agentic (no tool use, environment interaction, or multi-turn agent loop). Adjacent to existing PPO/GAE/GRPO foundations but outside the Agentic RL scope; no agent-specific contribution to retain.
candidates.suggested_note: Skipped: general RLVR/LLM-reasoning policy optimization (BPO), not agentic RL. Abstract-only; no code inspected.

candidates.title: From Pretraining to Proficiency: Real-World Subtask RL for Long-Horizon Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention
candidates.reason: Real-world robot manipulation RL (bimanual YAM, Franka). Out of scope for the Agentic RL (LLM agent) knowledge base; no LLM agent, tool use, or language-agent training. Not relevant to existing sources.
candidates.suggested_note: Skipped: robot manipulation subtask RL, out of Agentic RL scope.

candidates.title: RULER: Instance-aware Rubric Rewards for SVG Generation
candidates.reason: Rubric-based reward for SVG code generation using GRPO. Reward-hacking and rubric-reward themes are tangentially relevant to lilian-reward, but the task (SVG generation) is not agentic RL and the contribution is domain-specific. Not a fit for the Agentic RL KB.
candidates.suggested_note: Skipped: rubric-reward RL for SVG generation, not agentic RL. Abstract-only; no code inspected.

candidates.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
candidates.reason: Directly on-topic for Agentic RL: recursive self-improvement loop where an agent edits its own code, with transfer to held-out benchmarks and a reported reward-hacking reduction (55%->32%). Overlaps conceptually with existing KB items on recursive harness self-improvement (modularrsi, sol-pi, rrsi-regularized-recursive-self-improvem). Abstract-only; no code or reproduction verified. Claims about hidden evaluations and generalization require human reading before any archival.
candidates.suggested_note: Preprint (2026-09-22). AIDE^2: agent proposes edits to its own code, benchmarks modified versions on AI R&D tasks, keeps best on hidden evals; 8-day autonomous run, 7 successive improvements; transfer to 4 held-out benchmarks; reward-hacking rate 55%->32%. Abstract-only; not reproduced. Cross-check against modularrsi/sol-pi/rrsi before archiving.

candidates.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
candidates.reason: Directly on-topic: regularized harness self-improvement addressing overfitting of recursive evolution, with reported in-distribution and OOD gains and token-efficiency claims. Strong conceptual overlap with existing KB items modularrsi-modular-and-generalizable-rec and rrsi-regularized-recursive-self-improvem; possible duplicate/related-work risk. Abstract-only; code URL present but not verified (HTTP 200 would not be evidence of correctness). Requires human reading and dedup check.
candidates.suggested_note: Preprint (2026-09-21). RRSI: annealed edit budget + critic/pruner to favor reusable harness mechanisms over benchmark-specific ones; up to +14.1 in-distribution, +4.7 on 5 OOD benchmarks, 30% fewer policy tokens. Abstract-only; code link unverified. Dedup against modularrsi and rrsi-regularized-recursive-self-improvem before archiving.

candidates.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
candidates.reason: Adjacent to Agentic RL scope: long-horizon agentic task with external procedural memory, continual adaptation under noisy/unverifiable feedback, and matched-replay gating. Relevant to KB interests in memory, harness evolution, and reward hacking, but domain (graphic design) is narrower and no RL training is claimed (frozen model, no weight updates). Abstract-only; requires human reading to judge fit.
candidates.suggested_note: Preprint (2026-09-18). Designer-RSI: frozen frontier model + external procedural memory of natural-language skills; widening/deepening with matched replay gate; 5 rounds over 1,406 briefs; skill bank 76->139; GenEval2 success 72.7%->99.3%. Abstract-only; no weight updates. Adjacent, not core Agentic RL.

candidates.title: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
candidates.reason: Off-scope for Agentic RL knowledge base: a computer-use benchmark for mechanical CAD in FreeCAD. Matches generic keywords (computer-use, long-horizon, benchmark) but does not address RL training, credit assignment, or agentic RL methodology. Not a duplicate of existing KB items.
candidates.suggested_note: Skip: CAD computer-use benchmark; not Agentic RL methodology. Revisit only if KB scope expands to GUI/CAD agent evaluation.

candidates.title: WorldCrafter: Consistent Video World Model with Implicit 3D-aware Memory
candidates.reason: Off-scope: video world model with implicit 3D-aware memory for scene exploration. Keyword matches (long-horizon, memory, exploration, distillation) are incidental; no RL training, policy optimization, or agentic RL content. Not a duplicate of existing KB items.
candidates.suggested_note: Skip: video world model; keyword overlap only. Not relevant to Agentic RL.

candidates.title: Towards Full Pipeline FP8 Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
candidates.reason: Directly relevant to the KB's RL-for-LLMs core (GRPO/DAPO are existing sources). Abstract claims a named instability (compounded FP8 quantization noise distorting importance ratios) and a mitigation (Calibrated Clipping) evaluated across GRPO/DAPO, 8B-32B, multiple FP8 granularities. Plausible and on-topic, but abstract-only; no code or reproduction checked. Requires human reading before any KB inclusion.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only. Claims full-pipeline FP8 RL instability traced to quantization noise distorting importance ratios, with Calibrated Clipping restoring BF16-comparable performance across GRPO/DAPO and 8B-32B. Verify: (1) whether the instability reproduces, (2) whether Calibrated Clipping is compared against TIS and other corrections, (3) whether code is released. Do not cite as established until reproduced.

candidates.title: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction
candidates.reason: Plausibly relevant to the KB's on-policy data/alignment and agent-trajectory themes (adjacent to instructgpt, dpo, agent-lightning). Abstract describes a token-level correction tool, a controlled study (52% median time reduction), and a released dataset/benchmark (Panda-CVL). Tooling and data artifacts could be useful, but abstract-only and the 52% figure is from a small controlled study. Requires human reading and artifact inspection.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only. Interactive token-level correction for on-policy SFT/preference data and agent trajectories; claims 52% median annotation-time reduction in a small controlled study and releases Panda-CVL dataset + benchmark. Verify: (1) study size and methodology, (2) whether Panda-CVL is actually available and licensed, (3) whether the on-policy distribution claim holds. Do not treat as validated tooling yet.

candidates.title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay
candidates.reason: Adjacent to the KB's long-horizon/planning/benchmark interests but not core Agentic RL training methodology. Large-scale gameplay dataset (5,000 hours, 21 games) and benchmark with offline/online tracks could be a useful evaluation resource later. Retain as a candidate without publishing; no KB note yet.
candidates.suggested_note: Abstract-only. Gameplay data + evaluation suite with multi-horizon instructions, offline and stepwise online tracks; claims 47 models evaluated. Adjacent, not core. Revisit only if the KB expands into game/embodied evaluation. Verify dataset release and licensing before any use.

candidates.title: From Pattern Recognizers to Personalized Companions: A Survey of Large Language Models in Mental Health
candidates.reason: Domain survey on LLMs in mental health. Off-scope for an Agentic RL knowledge base; the agent-architecture framing (profile/memory/reasoning/planning) is generic and does not add RL-specific evidence. Not a duplicate, but irrelevant to the KB's purpose.
candidates.suggested_note: Skip. Off-scope domain survey (mental-health LLMs). No Agentic RL training or methodology contribution relevant to this KB.

candidates.title: ShieldVLA: Feasibility-Aware Safety Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.reason: Robotics VLA safety-alignment paper (HJ reachability, safety critic, rubric-based VLM scores). Off-scope for an Agentic RL knowledge base focused on LLM agents; the RL content is robotics-specific and not transferable to the KB's themes. Not a duplicate, but irrelevant.
candidates.suggested_note: Skip. Off-scope robotics VLA safety alignment. No LLM-agentic-RL contribution relevant to this KB.

candidates.title: ACLArena: Agent Continue Learning in Multi-stage Post-training
candidates.reason: Directly relevant to Agentic RL: studies agent continual learning across multi-stage post-training, compares multi-teacher on-policy distillation, self-distilled fine-tuning, and model merging, and proposes an offline-replay + routed LoRA-expert RL recipe. Overlaps thematically with existing KB sources (dapo, gigpo, agent-lightning, mintrl-off-policy-intervention-can-boost) but is not a duplicate. Only the abstract was read; no code or reproduction verified.
candidates.suggested_note: New preprint (2026-09-21). Agent Continual Learning framework: sequential training pipeline, model-level and token-level forgetting/generalization analysis, comparison of multi-teacher on-policy distillation vs self-distilled FT vs model merging, plus an offline-replay + routed multi-LoRA-expert RL recipe. Abstract-only; claims unverified. Read in full before any KB promotion; check for overlap with dapo/gigpo/agent-lightning.

candidates.title: BI-Agent and BI-Bench: Towards Automating End-to-End Business Intelligence
candidates.reason: Plausibly on-topic: tool-augmented agent with SFT+RL post-training on synthesized trajectories, plus a new benchmark (BI-Bench). Relevant to the KB's tool-use/agent-training and benchmark threads (tau-bench, gaia, webarena). Not a duplicate. Abstract-only; benchmark construction and reported gains (up to 40/30 points) unverified.
candidates.suggested_note: New preprint (2026-09-16). End-to-end BI agent (BI-Agent) with tool-augmented decomposition (search/join/transform) and SFT+RL post-training from synthesized trajectories; introduces BI-Bench from real dashboards. Abstract-only; verify benchmark leakage, task construction, and RL setup before considering for KB.

candidates.title: Jev-Mem: System-One-Controlled Agentic Memory for Efficient AI Agents
candidates.reason: Agentic-memory architecture for long-horizon agents (System-One control plane + structured memory + System-Two reasoning). Adjacent to the KB's agent/memory and long-horizon interests (lilian-agent, agentic-survey) but not a duplicate. Abstract-only; reported LoCoMo score and latency/speedup claims unverified.
candidates.suggested_note: New preprint (2026-09-21). System-One/System-Two-inspired agentic memory: lightweight controller for memory typing/retrieval routing plus deliberative reasoning plane. Abstract-only; verify evaluation protocol and baselines. Peripheral to core Agentic RL training; review before any inclusion.

candidates.title: SteerDuplex: Steerable Duplex Speech Dialogue Models
candidates.reason: Full-duplex spoken dialogue model with steerability and two-stage RL. Domain (speech dialogue) is outside the Agentic RL scope of this KB; keyword matches (reward hacking, RL, benchmark) are incidental. Not a duplicate but not relevant.
candidates.suggested_note: Out of scope: speech-dialogue steerability, not Agentic RL. Skip unless the KB later expands to speech/duplex interaction.

candidates.title: Think Like a World Model, Act Like a VLA: Distilling World-Model Representations into Compact Robot Policies
candidates.reason: Vision-Language-Action robotics policy distillation from world-model features. Domain (robot manipulation/VLA) is outside the Agentic RL scope; keyword matches (policy, alignment, test-time compute) are incidental. Not a duplicate but not relevant.
candidates.suggested_note: Out of scope: VLA/robotics representation distillation, not Agentic RL. Skip unless the KB later adds embodied/robotics coverage.

candidates.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
candidates.reason: Directly on-topic for the KB's harness cluster (multi-harness, RRSI, SoL-Pi, harness-design study). Abstract claims harness distillation via agent-as-harness, transferring harness-induced behavior into weights so gains survive under a fixed target harness, with reported macro-average task success 23.3% -> 44.3% and 82.3% pattern recovery across 28 patterns. These are abstract-only claims; no code, no reproduction, and the action-space/information mismatch between source and target harness is a nontrivial methodological risk. Requires human reading before any archival as knowledge.
candidates.suggested_note: 2026-09-23: harness distillation via agent-as-harness; claims gains survive after removing the specialized harness (23.3% -> 44.3% macro-avg success; 82.3% recovery across 28 patterns). Abstract-only, not reproduced. Read for: how harness guidance is converted into target-harness demonstrations, and whether the fixed-target-harness evaluation is fair.

candidates.title: EDGEGEN: Improving Tool-Calling Agents Beyond Happy Paths with Synthetic Edge Case Generation
candidates.reason: Plausibly relevant to tool-calling agent training/evaluation and overlaps the existing tau-bench source. Abstract claims compliance-rule extraction from agent specs to generate database-grounded edge-case tasks, with finetuning gains of 2%-42% mean progress on tau2bench airline and harness-optimization gains of 10%/30% for Gemma-4-e4b. Abstract-only; the 'fully automated closed-loop, no human annotation' claim and the tau2bench variant naming need verification. More data-generation/eval than core RL methodology, so review rather than archive.
candidates.suggested_note: 2026-09-23: synthetic edge-case task generation from agent compliance rules; claims finetuning + harness-optimization gains on tau2bench airline. Abstract-only, not reproduced. Check: rule-extraction validity, whether generated tasks are verifiable, and relation to existing tau-bench source.

candidates.reason: Robotics manipulation / VLA and world-action-model 3D grounding (RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO-PRO, real robots). Outside the Agentic RL scope of this KB; keyword matches on 'long-horizon', 'policy', 'memory' are incidental. No overlap with existing sources.

candidates.suggested_note: Out of scope: persona/role-play simulation, not Agentic RL.
